title: 1952 AHSME Problem 8
statement: Two equal circles in the same plane cannot have the following number of common tangents:

solutions.text:
Two distinct equal circles have \(2\) common tangents when they intersect, \(3\) when externally tangent, and \(4\) when disjoint. They cannot be internally tangent, because internal tangency requires the center distance to equal the difference of the radii, which is \(0.\) At center distance \(0\) the equal circles coincide and have infinitely many common tangents.

Thus exactly \(1\) common tangent is impossible, so the correct answer is A.
hints: Consider intersecting, externally tangent, and disjoint equal circles
An internal tangency would require unequal radii unless the circles coincide
